title: Manali to Leh to Manali (9N/10D)
reportingPoint: The AC Volvo to Manali leaves Delhi around 8 PM on Day 0, with a dinner stop on the way. You can also join from Chandigarh or Manali. The exact pickup point is shared once your booking is confirmed.
highlights: Atal Tunnel and Baralacha La, into Lahaul on the Leh-Manali highway
Sarchu, a night under a million stars
Gata Loops and Tanglang La, a day of high passes into Leh
Khardung La (18,380 ft), then Diskit and the dunes
Turtuk, the last village on the Indo-Pak border
Pangong Tso, then Chang La at 17,800 ft
overview:
The great Himalayan loop: the Leh-Manali highway over Baralacha and Tanglang La, Sarchu under the stars, Khardung La and Nubra, Turtuk, Pangong Tso and Chang La, by bike or by car. It is a **9 Nights / 10 Days** fixed-departure group trip, Manali to Manali, with an AC Volvo from Delhi and back included and pickup from Delhi, Chandigarh or Manali. Stays are in double or triple rooms in hotels and camps, with 15 meals across the trip.

Travel in a sitting coach (SIC) by Tempo Traveller, ride a Royal Enfield Himalayan solo or with a pillion, or bring your own bike. An oxygen cylinder rides in the car 24x7, with mechanical backup and a team captain throughout. Prices start at ₹22,500 per person on triple sharing riding pillion on an RE Himalayan, or ₹33,500 by SIC (5% GST extra). Reserve your seat with ₹8,000 and pay the rest 24 hours before boarding. Batches run every week in the summer season, late May to early October, when the Leh-Manali highway is open; call us for 2027 dates.

itinerary.title: Delhi to Manali
itinerary.content: Depart Delhi around 8 PM in an AC Volvo, with a dinner stop on the way.

itinerary.title: Manali: arrival and acclimatisation
itinerary.content:
Check in, freshen up, breakfast and a short trip briefing.
Self-explore Manali: Vashisht Temple, Hadimba Temple, Mall Road and Jogini Waterfall.
Early night at the hotel to rest for the adventure ahead.

itinerary.title: Manali to Sarchu
itinerary.content:
Breakfast, check out and start the famous Leh-Manali highway.
Through the Atal Tunnel into Lahaul, past Darcha and over Baralacha Pass.
Reach Sarchu by evening for a night under a million stars at the camp.

itinerary.title: Sarchu to Leh
itinerary.content:
A day of high passes: the Gata Loops, Nakee La and Lachung La.
Lunch on the More plains at Pang.
Over Tanglang La into Leh. Evening free to acclimatise; overnight in Leh.

itinerary.title: Leh to Nubra via Khardung La
itinerary.content:
After breakfast, ride over Khardung La (18,380 ft).
Visit Diskit Monastery and its 100 ft Buddha; camel and ATV rides are at your own cost.
Check in to the campsite for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Nubra to Turtuk and back
itinerary.content:
Head to Turtuk, the last village of India on the Indo-Pak border, famous for its apricots.
Walk the village, sun-bask by the Shyok River and visit the Balti Museum.
Back to Nubra for dinner and an overnight stay.

itinerary.title: Nubra to Pangong Tso
itinerary.content:
Check out after breakfast and head to Pangong Lake, famous from 3 Idiots.
Check in to cottages, explore the lakeside and capture surreal views.
A warm dinner and the night sky over the lake (weather permitting).

itinerary.title: Pangong Tso to Leh via Chang La
itinerary.content:
Over Chang La (17,800 ft) to Leh, visiting Shey Palace and Thiksey Monastery.
Overnight in Leh.

itinerary.title: Leh to Jispa / Sarchu
itinerary.content:
Ride from Leh to Jispa or Sarchu.
Overnight at the camp.

itinerary.title: Back to Manali and the overnight bus
itinerary.content: On to Manali, and board the overnight bus to Delhi.

itinerary.title: Arrive in Delhi
itinerary.content: Arrive in Delhi. The tour ends here.

faqs.q: Where does the trip start and end?
faqs.a: The AC Volvo to Manali leaves Delhi around 8 PM on Day 0, and you can also be picked up from Chandigarh or Manali. The loop runs Manali to Manali, and the overnight bus brings you back to Delhi on Day 10.

faqs.q: What are the travel options and what do they cost?
faqs.a: Per person on triple sharing: sitting coach (SIC) ₹33,500, RE Himalayan solo rider ₹47,500, RE Himalayan with pillion ₹22,500, your own bike solo ₹35,500 and your own bike with a pillion ₹32,500. On the own-bike options, double occupancy is ₹3,000 per person extra. 5% GST is extra.

Summer season only, from late May to early October, when the Leh-Manali highway is open. Batches leave every week (for example 28 May to 7 June and 4 to 14 June, through 26 September to 5 October 2027). Call us for 2027 dates.

Double or triple rooms in hotels and camps, 15 meals, the Volvo between Delhi and Manali, bike rental for 6 days with fuel (bike option) or travel Manali to Manali by Tempo Traveller (SIC), mechanical backup, an oxygen cylinder 24x7, all inner line permits, a team captain and riding gear.

5% GST, unspecified meals, room heater charges, entry and monument fees, personal expenses and tips, extra days due to weather or snow road blocks, any damage to the bike except engine damage, and costs from medical emergencies.

faqs.q: How do I book and pay?
faqs.a: Pick your batch and option, then call or WhatsApp us on +91 88008 41209. Reserve your seat with an advance of ₹8,000 per person by UPI, GPay, PhonePe, Paytm or net banking, and pay the balance 24 hours before boarding. 5% GST is extra on the trip price.
The ₹8,000 advance is not refunded under any circumstances. The balance is due 24 hours before boarding, and pending payments may cancel the booking. Bookings can't be transferred.
